evaluation.final_reason: The group moved from complaints to partial agreements: they agreed in principle to set "a simple cooking and washing-up rota" and to "chip in for dish soap and gas" (Agent A: "Can we set a simple cooking and washing-up rota?"; Agent A: "...we can chip in for dish soap and gas."). substantive_insights: Agent A is willing to take on more practical burden (washing, running extractor) and contributes supplies, which helps de-escalate the immediate smell/cleanliness issues.

Group-level agreement emerged at the level of principle (rota + shared costs) but not at the level of implementation (no schedule or method for contributions), leaving a small remaining coordination problem.

The extractor was the specific behavior that directly addressed the smell complaint and was explicitly agreed to, showing that small behavioral commitments can resolve the most salient immediate harm even if formal rules are deferred.
